message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo are abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA). PGS000753 is preferred because it provides a relatively clean, PRS-comparable effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) from a selected European validation record and uses a straightforward covariate set (age, sex, PCs), whereas other candidates either provide only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS003973 C-index 0.882 with age/sex; PGS001784 full-model AUROC 0.868 with extensive covariates) or non-AUC metrics without clear PRS-only context. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct-match in the sense that they target alcohol dependence/AUD-related endpoints, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and the strength/clarity of reported validation evidence. PGS002738 is the most directly aligned to the target trait at the concept level (trait_efo: alcohol dependence; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: Alcohol use disorder) and provides an interpretable case-control style validation summary (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) with multiple validation records (record_count=4), suggesting some robustness. The main limitation is that key performance fields (AUC/R2) are not reported and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability and raising uncertainty about evaluation context. The alternative direct-EFO models (PGS000201/PGS000202) report a DSM-5 criteria count phenotype (log-transformed) under a broader label (“Problematic alcohol use”) and provide ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) with explicit covariates, but their trait_efo is ‘alcohol dependence measurement’ rather than alcohol dependence itself and their reported effects are modest; PGS002739 is ancestry-specific (AFR evaluation) and gene-based with fewer variants, making it less generally supported from the provided context. Overall, PGS002738 is preferred on endpoint alignment plus the clearest risk-discrimination metric, but evidence remains incomplete, so the direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001777","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches by trait_efo (alcoholic liver cirrhosis). PGS001777 is best supported on endpoint fidelity and interpretability: it is a disease-focused score for alcohol-related cirrhosis with a clear discrimination metric (AUROC 0.671 in European validation) and a strong risk-gradient summary (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18). However, the evidence is not strong enough for a high-quality designation because the reported performance is a full-model AUROC (not clearly PRS-only), covariates are listed as unknown, and validation is relatively small (n=1,390). Competing models have limitations that prevent a clearly superior choice: PGS000704 reports a higher C-index (0.711) but it is also a full-model metric with covariate adjustment and comes from a broad biomarker genetics study (less clearly disease-focused), while PGS004913 is disease-focused but reports only a small PRS R² (0.029) and no AUC/C-index, making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo matches). Among models with clearly reported, comparable PRS-only performance, the snpnet UKB models (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) provide explicit PGS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.59) and PGS R² (~0.012–0.013) plus incremental AUROC, whereas several newer I20/PheCode models (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527 and PGS00504x/PGS00505x) lack PRS-only metrics and/or have unclear training details (often 'N/A') and report only full-model C-index or an OR, limiting direct comparability. Within the snpnet set, PGS001262 has the strongest selected European full-model AUROC (0.80729) and the highest incremental AUROC (0.0098) with a directly stated doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint, making it the best-supported pick from the visible evidence. Limitation: the best-supported choice is still sub-optimal because the strongest-looking discrimination is for a covariate-including full model (age/sex/PCs/array), while PRS-only performance remains modest and close across candidates; additionally, multiple alternative direct-endpoint models exist with incomplete or non-comparable performance reporting, preventing a high-confidence single clear winner."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo/trait_reported, with generally good endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported is ankylosing spondylitis for most; one is explicitly time-to-event). Among models with clearly reported, PRS-comparable discrimination metrics in the record, PGS001267 provides both PRS-only AUROC (0.72651 with CI) and full-model AUROC (0.74328 with CI) in a European validation record, with standard covariates (age, sex, array type, PCs) and multiple validation records available. Competing UKB portability models (PGS001876, PGS002089) report only partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R², making direct comparability to the snpnet AUROC-based records limited from the visible evidence. The Taiwanese EAS-focused models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report higher full-model AUROC (~0.76–0.79) but have small validation sample size (n=1,298), unknown covariates, and no PRS-only metrics shown, reducing confidence in selecting them as the best-supported overall direct-match choice from this context. Remaining limitation: PGS001268 (time-to-event) has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.74878) than PGS001267, but it targets a different endpoint definition (TTE), so without a stated preference for incident/time-to-event vs generic case-control disease risk, the best pick is not unequivocal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the target trait (aortic stenosis) are present: PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, and PGS005256 all have trait_efo including aortic stenosis and phenotyping_reported as incident aortic stenosis (for PGS005255/PGS005256 the trait_reported is a valve-function measurement but the endpoint still states incident aortic stenosis). Among these, PGS005252 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is explicitly labeled Aortic stenosis, uses an incident aortic stenosis endpoint, and is the only direct-match model with a reported discrimination metric in the selected validation record (C-index 0.87) alongside an effect size (HR 1.92), with EUR development and EUR evaluation specified. Main limitation: performance reporting is not directly comparable across candidates here because PGS005254/PGS005255/PGS005256 report HRs (with CIs) but no AUC/C-index, and PGS005252’s reported metric is a full-model C-index with multiple clinical covariates (potential packaging), while PRS-only performance is not shown—so the preference is based on the presence of a clear validation discrimination metric and endpoint alignment rather than clean PRS-only comparability."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 (\"Arthritis (nos)\", trait_efo=arthritis) and ICD10 M13 \"Other arthritis\" models (PGS004477, PGS004547). PGS001135 is the most directly aligned to the generic target via both trait_efo=arthritis and phenotyping_reported=\"Arthritis (nos)\", and it provides interpretable PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.539; PGS R2 0.00291) plus a selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.674, incremental AUROC 0.00314). However, the available direct-match options are heterogeneous in endpoint definition (\"arthritis (nos)\" vs ICD10 M13 \"Other arthritis\") and several newer M13 models report only an OR without comparable PRS-only metrics or AUC, limiting evidence-based ranking; therefore the direct-match recommendation is present but not clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for asthma are present (multiple models with trait_efo=asthma). Among the listed candidates, PGS001344 (snpnet; asthma diagnosed by doctor) has strong endpoint fidelity for generic asthma risk (doctor-diagnosed asthma) and shows the best reported discrimination in the provided set with a European validation record (full_model AUROC 0.66621 with CI 0.65552–0.67691; also provides PRS-only AUROC 0.64568 and PRS-only R2 0.05973). Competing direct-match models either report lower AUROC (e.g., PGS001341/PGS001343/PGS001346 ~0.636 full-model AUROC; PGS001782 full-model AUROC 0.659 but without PRS-only AUROC/R2 and with only one record) or lack comparable classification metrics (many report only incremental R2 or partial correlation). However, the recommendation remains sub-optimal because performance reporting is heterogeneous across candidates (many lack PRS-only metrics or AUROC), and several models target different asthma endpoints (incident, pediatric, time-to-event), making direct comparability imperfect from the visible metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=atopic eczema, but several have endpoint-mismatch limitations: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients (not general atopic eczema risk), and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in Canadian cohorts with only full-model metrics reported (AUROC=0.93, R²=0.49) that include covariates, making PRS-only contribution unclear. Among the remaining incident atopic dermatitis endpoints, PGS002755 and PGS004587 both report time-to-event effect sizes (HR high vs low PRS 1.249 vs 1.153, respectively) in European validation; PGS002755 also uses a genome-wide PRS-CS construction with very large variant coverage (1,090,702), which is a positive signal for polygenic signal capture. However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because neither model provides PRS-only discrimination/calibration metrics (e.g., PRS-only AUROC/R²), and the HRs are not directly comparable to AUROC-based candidates; thus the selection is based on limited, heterogeneous performance reporting rather than a clean, directly comparable PRS metric."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in the provided context because it targets atrial fibrillation directly (phenotyping_reported: \"Atrial fibrillation\"), is derived from a large AF-focused meta-analysis (Nat Genet; training_development_cohorts list spans many cohorts), and reports strong discrimination in the selected European validation record (C-index 0.8718 with CI 0.8657–0.878; validation n=52,757). Main limitation: several other direct AF models also report high full-model concordance/C-index (e.g., PGS005067 C-index 0.8276; PGS005065 C-index 0.8253; PGS005061 C-index 0.8229; PGS005063 C-index 0.8233), but their endpoints are PheCode-based and their reported effect sizes/metrics are not directly comparable across studies due to differing covariate sets and metric types; additionally, many candidates lack clean PRS-only performance metrics, so the preference for PGS005168 rests primarily on endpoint fidelity plus the strongest reported European validation performance in this context rather than a fully harmonized PRS-only comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct-match at the EFO level (each includes atrial flutter), but only PGS001263 is endpoint-specific to atrial flutter in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported (\"Atrial flutter\"), whereas PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 are broader combined endpoints (\"atrial fibrillation and flutter\"; PGS001339 also uses a time-to-event definition). PGS001263 also provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 and PGS R2 0.025 in European validation) plus full-model AUROC with covariates, while the 2022 portability-study models (PGS001841/PGS002050) do not report AUROC/R2 here (only partial-r), limiting direct comparability. Remaining limitation: evidence is UK Biobank–centric across all candidates and the best-supported choice is based on metadata/performance fields shown (single selected European validation record), with no external-cohort performance presented; additionally, PGS001339 is a close competitor with similar PRS-only performance but less specific phenotype alignment."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS000327, PGS002790). PGS000327 has stronger endpoint fidelity: phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder,” matching the target trait, whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn),” which weakens confidence that its reported ASD label reflects a clean ASD endpoint. On the available validation evidence, PGS000327 also shows higher reported performance (full_model_r2=0.0245 with OR=1.33 [1.30–1.36]) than PGS002790 (partial R²=0.00546; no effect sizes shown). Both are EUR-only in evaluation, so ancestry does not differentiate them here. Overall, PGS000327 is the best-supported direct-match, but confidence is limited because neither model provides PRS-only AUC/R² and the reported R² values are not clearly comparable across records (full-model vs partial R²), leaving some metric ambiguity."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 20 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity and the most informative reported validation performance. Among models with comparable reported metrics, PGS000452 (GWAS Hits; 28 variants) shows the strongest full-model discrimination and risk gradient in its selected European validation record (full_model_auc=0.632 with CI 0.616–0.647; OR=1.663 [1.57–1.761]; top 1% vs rest OR=3.61 [2.53–5.15]) with standard covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and a direct BCC endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma). Close competitors include PGS000454 (very similar AUC=0.632 and OR=1.661) and PGS000119 (higher AUC=0.64 but from a different study family and with less directly comparable reporting structure), making the choice not uniquely decisive from the visible metadata alone; additionally, most records report only full-model AUC (not PRS-only), limiting clean comparability across candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001824","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo/phenotyping. PGS001824 and PGS002032 have the highest endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported: \"Disorders of bilirubin excretion\"; trait_efo: bilirubin metabolism disease), whereas PGS000924 targets a broader composite endpoint (\"Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism\" time-to-event), making it less specific to bilirubin metabolism disease. Between the two bilirubin-excretion models, the visible evidence does not show any performance advantage (both report the same partial correlation 0.0716 with similar CIs and lack AUROC/R²), so they are near-tied; PGS001824 is selected only as a conservative choice given its simpler/sparser construction (22 variants vs 19,768) with no demonstrated performance loss in the provided metrics. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because key comparable performance fields (e.g., PRS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for the top endpoint-aligned models, leaving limited evidence to make a clearly strong recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches by trait label/EFO (bipolar disorder; bipolar I; bipolar II) and share the same study family (same publication, SDPR method, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, PGC training cohort), so there is no clear differentiator from transportability or methodology. Endpoint fidelity is a key concern: the reported phenotyping/validation endpoints are not bipolar disorder case-control outcomes (they are cognitive/behavioral measures such as pattern comparison, DSM5 depression behavior, and sluggish cognitive tempo), which weakens confidence that these are optimized/validated as bipolar disorder risk scores despite the trait labels. Reported performance is limited to small partial R² values with no AUC/PRS-only metrics, and the validation sample sizes are modest and similar. Given the target is generic ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is the closest concept match (not subtype-specific), but the evidence is insufficient to call it a clearly high-quality direct-match choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches at the broad level of “blood coagulation disease,” but they differ in endpoint specificity and in the availability/clarity of comparable performance evidence. PGS001033 aligns directly to the target EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) and its phenotyping_reported is a coagulation-defect disease endpoint (“TTE other coagulation defects”), with explicit validation performance reported (AUROC with CI; PRS-only AUROC/R²; covariates listed). In contrast, PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the broad blood coagulation disease EFO) and only report partial correlation (no AUROC/R²), making performance less directly comparable from the visible metadata. The main limitation is that PGS001033 appears to be a time-to-event endpoint for “other coagulation defects,” which may not fully cover the intended breadth of “blood coagulation disease,” and its model is extremely sparse (variants_number=1), so despite having clearer metrics it is not an unambiguously high-quality broad coagulation-disease PRS from the provided evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001336","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match models for breast carcinoma are present (multiple models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma / trait_reported=Breast cancer). Among the visible candidates, PGS001336 is a direct breast cancer endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Breast cancer) with a clearly reported PRS-only discrimination metric (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.59627) and a corresponding full-model AUROC (0.80961) in European validation, which is more interpretable than many other candidates that only report full-model AUROC or omit PRS-only metrics. A key limitation is that several other direct breast cancer models also show strong full-model performance (e.g., PGS000007 full_model_auc=0.78; PGS000332 C-index=0.75) but lack PRS-only metrics, making cross-model comparison on a PRS-comparable axis incomplete; additionally, PGS001336’s reported full-model performance includes covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), so the PRS-only metric is the cleaner comparator but is only modestly discriminative."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000316","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and the interpretability of reported performance. PGS000316 has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease) and reports a strong European validation AUROC (0.879, CI 0.87–0.888) with a very large validation sample size (n=379,767), making its performance evidence comparatively robust within the provided metadata. PGS000040 reports an even higher AUROC (0.90) but the record shows covariates as Unknown and a much smaller validation sample (n=2,476), and several other candidates (e.g., PGS001856/PGS002067) lack AUROC and only provide partial correlation, limiting direct comparability. A remaining limitation is that PGS000316’s reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and covariates are listed as Unknown, so some uncertainty remains about how much of the discrimination is attributable to the PRS alone versus model packaging."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001299","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo: cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported: cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Among them, PGS001299 provides the most informative and PRS-comparable performance reporting because it includes both PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.55215; PGS R2 0.00263) and full-model metrics (full_model AUROC 0.76761; incremental AUROC 0.00676) from a selected European validation record, enabling clearer interpretation than models that report only covariate-inclusive C-index/AUROC. However, the overall evidence remains sub-optimal because several other direct-match models report only full-model discrimination (e.g., PGS000073/PGS000784 AUROC ~0.745 with extensive covariates; PGS003428 C-index 0.613; PGS005165 C-index 0.566), making cross-model comparison difficult and leaving uncertainty about which score has the strongest standalone genetic signal for cervical cancer."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001174","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (or a closely overlapping endpoint). PGS001174 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has the clearest endpoint specificity (phenotyping_reported: time-to-event cholelithiasis; trait_efo: cholelithiasis) and it is the only candidate with explicit, interpretable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.62342; full-model AUROC 0.66706 with CI; PRS-only R² 0.02808) in a European validation record, enabling a like-for-like assessment. Competing direct candidates (PGS001861, PGS002072) target a broader combined phenotype (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and report only partial correlation rather than AUROC/R²; the newer K80-specific models (PGS004476, PGS004546) and the East Asian-focused model (PGS005150) provide only single effect-size summaries (OR/β) without comparable validation performance fields and have ‘Unknown’ covariates for the K80 models. Main limitation: evidence is incomplete and heterogeneous across candidates (different endpoints and non-comparable metrics), so while PGS001174 is the most evidence-supported pick, the choice is not decisively high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct EFO matches to chronic kidney disease, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable the reported performance is. PGS002237 is the most clearly disease-focused CKD score in this set: it targets a clinically specific CKD endpoint (stage 3+; eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a CKD-focused Nat Med study explicitly aiming to predict CKD across ancestries, with multi-ancestry evaluation reported. However, the visible performance is primarily a full-model AUROC (0.78 in European validation) with substantial clinical covariates included, and there is no PRS-only AUROC/R² shown here, limiting comparability and raising packaging/adjustment concerns. Competing direct-match options either have weaker/less relevant endpoints (e.g., eGFR proxy in PGS000728; diabetes-subtype phenotype in PGS000859; secondhand-smoke-exposure-conditioned endpoint in PGS004224), modest PRS-only discrimination (PGS001272), or are benchmarking-family models with relatively low full-model AUROCs (~0.59) and no covariates (PGS003988–PGS004158). Given these trade-offs and incomplete PRS-only reporting for the strongest disease-aligned model, the best-supported choice is PGS002237 but with only moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001783 is best supported by the visible evidence because it targets the exact disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: \"Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease\"), uses a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS-auto; 884,139 variants), and reports comparatively stronger PRS-comparable performance (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) alongside a reported AUROC of 0.74 in European validation. However, the overall direct-match evidence remains sub-optimal because several competing COPD models exist with similar endpoint alignment but non-comparable or incomplete performance reporting (e.g., PGS004466/PGS004536 provide only ORs; PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334 provide PRS-only AUROC ~0.54–0.55 but also full-model AUROCs that are not directly comparable to PRS-only), and key details such as incremental metrics/covariate cleanliness are missing or inconsistent across candidates, limiting a high-confidence single best choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the target level (cirrhosis of liver), but several are subtype-specific to alcoholic cirrhosis (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) or have phenotype/label inconsistencies (PGS000776 is labeled cirrhosis but is described as alcohol-related variants and phenotyped as incident cirrhosis in an at-risk NAFLD population). Among the two explicitly generic cirrhosis models (PGS000726, PGS004621), PGS004621 has the strongest visible endpoint alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both 'Cirrhosis'), uses a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS) with broad variant coverage (1,089,806 variants), and reports a representative validation AUROC of 0.68 in European ancestry. However, confidence is not high because the reported performance is full-model AUROC (not clearly PRS-only), and PGS000726 provides only OR-based metrics without AUC/R2, making cross-candidate performance comparability limited from the available metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034) with identical trait_efo alignment to the target and the same phenotyping_reported endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), so endpoint fidelity does not distinguish them. PGS002034 is selected as a slight preference because it achieves marginally higher partial-r and uses a substantially larger variant set (32,552 vs 45), but this is a weak differentiator given the near-identical performance and lack of additional PRS-only AUC/R2 or other discriminating metrics in the provided records."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both explicitly aligned to the target via trait_reported/trait_efo and with phenotyping_reported = \"Corneal dystrophy\" (good endpoint fidelity, no mismatch visible). However, the evidence remains limited because only partial-r is available (no AUC/R2, no classification metrics), and the two models are otherwise very similar, so the direct-match recommendation is not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are present (many models with trait_efo=coronary artery disease). Among the visible candidates, PGS000013 has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: “Coronary artery disease”), a clearly reported European validation record, and comparatively strong reported discrimination in that record (full_model AUROC 0.81; also reports a PRS-comparable metric: pgs_only_r2=0.04). However, the evidence remains insufficient for a clearly high-confidence ‘best’ choice because several other direct CAD/CHD models show equal-or-higher full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS000018 AUROC 0.89; PGS001780 AUROC 0.913), but these are not directly comparable on a PRS-only axis in the provided metadata and may reflect different covariate packaging/endpoint definitions (e.g., incident vs prevalent, recurrent events, age-restricted CAD, or CHD vs CAD). With these unresolved comparability limitations, PGS000013 is a reasonable, well-supported direct CAD candidate but not uniquely decisive from the visible context."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005170","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match dementia candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=dementia / all-cause dementia). PGS005170 is the best-supported direct-match option in the provided context because it has high endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_reported: all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia) and uses an explicitly integrative/ensemble-style construction (integrative PRS of 24 component PRSs), which the provided domain_knowledge flags as a consistent positive predictor of real-world performance. Main limitation: several other direct dementia models also have strong endpoint alignment and report competitive discrimination in UKB-derived evaluations (e.g., snpnet time-to-event dementia models and GenoBoost all-cause dementia models with high full-model AUROC), but the context does not provide fully comparable PRS-only metrics across these candidates, and some reported AUROCs appear to be full-model (covariate-including) rather than PGS-only, leaving residual ambiguity in head-to-head ranking."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002036","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for depressive disorder are present (multiple models with trait_efo major depressive disorder or depressive disorder). Among models with phenotyping_reported explicitly matching a generic depression endpoint (PGS001829, PGS002036), PGS002036 is better supported by the visible evidence because it targets the same endpoint label (“Depression”), uses a modern genome-wide method (LDpred2) with broad variant coverage (807,338 variants), and shows the strongest reported PRS-comparable metric among these two (partial-r 0.0556 vs 0.0323 for PGS001829) in the same study context and covariate set.
